theory.intro: A **minimal connector problem** uses a minimum spanning tree to link sites at the lowest total distance or cost. It finds the cheapest network to connect all locations, such as laying pipes or cables.
facts: A **minimal connector** links all sites in a network with the lowest total edge weight (distance or cost).
Multiply total MST length by the unit rate to find cost: $\text{Total Cost} = \text{MST length} \times \text{unit rate}$.
The **shortest path** between two specific vertices is not always part of the minimum spanning tree.
A minimal connector connects every site to a shared system, but may not provide direct routes between individual pairs.
steps: Construct the minimum spanning tree for the network
Calculate the total weight by summing the selected edges
Interpret the result with units and calculate any total cost

workedExamples.question_text:
The table shows direct distances, in kilometres, between four towns. A railway network will connect all four towns at a construction cost of $\$60\,000$ per kilometre. Draw a minimum spanning tree and calculate the minimum construction cost.

| From/To | $A$ | $B$ | $C$ | $D$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $A$ | – | 4.2 | 6.4 | 3.1 |
| $B$ | 4.2 | – | 5.3 | 2.2 |
| $C$ | 6.4 | 5.3 | – | 4.6 |
| $D$ | 3.1 | 2.2 | 4.6 | – |

A minimum spanning tree connecting six picnic areas has five path lengths: $20\text{ m}$, $25\text{ m}$, $30\text{ m}$, $35\text{ m}$ and $40\text{ m}$. Paving costs $\$90$ per metre. Calculate the minimum total path length and paving cost.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The minimum spanning tree is supplied, so sum its five edge weights.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Minimum length} &=20+25+30+35+40\\&=150\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
Multiply by the paving rate.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Minimum cost} &=150\times90\\&=\$13\,500\end{aligned}$

foundation.question_text:
Fibre optic broadband cable is being laid to connect four suburban hubs.
The minimum spanning tree of the network has a total length of $18\text{ km}$.
If laying the cable costs $\$15\,000$ per kilometre, calculate the total cost to connect all four hubs.

A botanical park is paving paths to connect four picnic areas $A, B, C, D$.
The minimum spanning tree of the path network has a total length of $250\text{ metres}$.
If paving costs $\$80$ per metre, find the total cost of paving the minimal connector path system.

The table shows the driving distances, in kilometres, between four regional schools $A, B, C, D$.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} \text{From/To} & A & B & C & D \\ \hline A & - & 12 & 15 & 8 \\ B & 12 & - & 9 & 14 \\ C & 15 & 9 & - & 11 \\ D & 8 & 14 & 11 & - \end{array}$
Calculate the minimum total length of road required to connect all four schools.

Power lines are being installed to connect six streetlights in a new residential estate.
The minimum spanning tree contains five cable segments with lengths $45\text{ m}, 60\text{ m}, 55\text{ m}, 40\text{ m}$, and $50\text{ m}$.
Determine the minimum total length of power cable needed.

An irrigation pipeline links five farm paddocks.
The minimum spanning tree length is $340\text{ metres}$.
If heavy-duty pipe costs $\$45$ per metre, calculate the total cost of the irrigation pipeline.

development.question_text:
The distance table shows the direct distances, in kilometres, between five regional mining sites $M_1, M_2, M_3, M_4, M_5$.
$\begin{array}{c|ccccc} \text{From/To} & M_1 & M_2 & M_3 & M_4 & M_5 \\ \hline M_1 & - & 14 & 20 & - & 10 \\ M_2 & 14 & - & 12 & 18 & - \\ M_3 & 20 & 12 & - & 8 & 15 \\ M_4 & - & 18 & 8 & - & 16 \\ M_5 & 10 & - & 15 & 16 & - \end{array}$
A freight railway line is to be built linking all five sites at a cost of $\$50\,000$ per kilometre.
Determine the minimum total cost of the rail network.

development.solution_text:
1. **Construct the minimum spanning tree for the network**
Select $CE$, $BF$, $DE$, $BC$ and $FA$. These connect all six villages without a cycle.
2. **Calculate the total weight by summing the selected edges**
$\text{Total road to clear} = 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 6 = 24\text{ km}$.
3. **Interpret the result with units and calculate any total cost**
The minimum total length of road to clear is $24\text{ km}$.

development.question_text:
An offshore wind farm consists of five wind turbines $T_1, T_2, T_3, T_4, T_5$ and one offshore substation $S$.
The minimum spanning tree connects all turbines and the substation with $32\text{ km}$ of subsea electrical cable.
If subsea cabling costs $\$1.2\text{ million}$ per kilometre, calculate the total cabling cost for the wind farm.

The distance table shows pipe lengths, in metres, required between four agricultural sprinkler stations $P, Q, R, S$.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} \text{From/To} & P & Q & R & S \\ \hline P & - & 24 & 32 & 18 \\ Q & 24 & - & 16 & 28 \\ R & 32 & 16 & - & 22 \\ S & 18 & 28 & 22 & - \end{array}$
Find the minimum total length of piping required to connect all four sprinkler stations.

A cloud datacenter cluster contains six server racks $R_1, R_2, R_3, R_4, R_5, R_6$.
A high-speed primary optical link between $R_1$ and $R_2$ ($5\text{ metres}$) has already been installed.
If the minimum spanning tree of the entire cluster containing this link has other segment lengths of $3\text{ m}, 4\text{ m}, 6\text{ m}$, and $7\text{ m}$, find the total length of optical cable in the completed network.

mastery.question_text:
A regional telecommunications network links seven towns with fibre optic cable.
The minimum spanning tree contains six cable links with distances $13\text{ km}, 16\text{ km}, 19\text{ km}, 23\text{ km}, 26\text{ km}$, and $31\text{ km}$.
Installation costs $\$42\,000$ per kilometre for every link.
Calculate the minimum total cost of installing the fibre optic network.
mastery.solution_text:
The minimum spanning tree is already given through its six link lengths.
2. **Calculate the total weight by summing the selected edges**
$\text{MST length} = 13 + 16 + 19 + 23 + 26 + 31 = 128\text{ km}$.
3. **Interpret the result with units and calculate any total cost**
$\text{Total Cost} = 128 \times 42\,000 = \$5\,376\,000$.

1. **Construct the minimum spanning tree for the network**
Select $GE$, $AG$, $DE$, $GC$, $CB$ and $AF$. These connect all seven towns without a cycle.
2. **Calculate the total weight by summing the selected edges**
$\text{Total distance} = 6 + 8 + 9 + 10 + 11 + 12 = 56\text{ km}$.
3. **Interpret the result with units and calculate any total cost**
The minimum total length of road to clear is $56\text{ km}$.
